rationale: Evidence: every development trial so far ended off track. The best run (iteration 2, score 132.0) had progress 0.45 on the oval, 0.27 on the s-bend and 0.16 on the slalom. Max error sat at about 0.06 m in every track and seed, which is the off-track limit. RMS error was about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation rose with kp (0.25 in the s-bend, 0.27 on the oval), and the oval's one finish came from the high-gain run. The widened sensor span and 16 mm footprint in iteration 2 clearly helped: line-loss events fell from 1.0 to 0.05 on the oval and 0.65 on the s-bend. The remaining failure looks like overshoot and oscillation in the steering loop, which take the robot past 0.06 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4), which is 0.06 for any allowed body width, so body width cannot buy margin. Changes: keep the iteration-2 geometry exactly (5 sensors at x = -0.06 to +0.06, y = 0.05, 16 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12, wheel_radius 0.03, body 0.18 x 0.12, mass 0.8). This isolates the controller. Reduce kp from 3.0 to 2.5 to lower the overshoot that drives the oscillation. Raise kd from 0.4 to 0.7 to damp the faster signal changes; iteration 1 raised kd to 0.6 but also changed other things, so this is not a clean test. Keep base_speed at 1.3 and ki at 0, and keep line_loss as last_direction, since line loss is now rare. Expected result: lower steering oscillation and max error held under 0.06 m, so the robot stays on track longer and progress rises above about 0.3 on the development tracks. Finishing within 3 s is still uncertain. If the oscillation falls but progress stalls, the next step is a speed increase.
